content.title: About
content.content: Pad Thai is a classic Thai stir‑fried rice noodle dish made with egg, tofu, shrimp or chicken, bean sprouts, peanuts and lime. It is cooked quickly over high heat, and the sauce balances sweet, sour and mild heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish gained worldwide fame in the 1970s thanks to a Thai tourism campaign.
Traditional Pad Thai is served with a lime wedge and crushed peanuts that diners add to taste.
The authentic recipe uses tamarind paste, palm sugar and fish sauce rather than regular white sugar.
There are many regional variations: some add extra seafood, others rely solely on tofu and vegetables.
Pad Thai is often called Thailand’s national street food, though the country has many other popular dishes.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Tofu, eggs and shrimp provide high‑quality plant and animal protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts and vegetable oils supply monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Lime and bean sprouts are high in vitamin C, which boosts immunity and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from bean sprouts and rice noodles promotes healthy gut function and satiety.

items.title: Low in gluten
items.content: Rice noodles are naturally gluten‑free, making the dish suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts commonly used in Pad Thai can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce and fish sauce add significant salt; those with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Spicy ingredients
items.content: Chili peppers and chili paste may irritate the stomach of people with sensitive digestive systems.

items.title: Additive concerns
items.content: Some pre‑made sauces contain artificial flavors and preservatives that may not be suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Pad Thai hot, straight from the wok. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the top, sprinkle with crushed peanuts, and add extra chili if desired. It can be eaten with chopsticks or a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed within 2–3 hours of cooking. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours; reheat quickly over high heat and add a splash of soy sauce to revive the flavor.
